subject: Allocation rotation proposal — porting windows and deal handoff for BrightEdge (DEAL-8421)
body:
From: Sam Liao <sam@brightedge.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-09-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: Q4 ramp: short-term flexibility request for dedicated capacity

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Brief recap and a small ask: BrightEdge has two campaigns that will spike token throughput in October and mid-November. We committed to a predictable latency envelope in the deal, but the exact traffic shape is bursty (many short, high-QPS windows).

Can Redwood support a modest "porting" arrangement where we temporarily shift 20% of our committed GPU slots to a shared burst pool for 6–12 hour windows on specific dates? We need this only for about 8 discrete windows in Q4.

If this isn't possible, we need to discuss temporary credits or a short-term SLA exception.

Sam
Customer Success Manager
BrightEdge

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
To: Sam Liao <sam@brightedge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-09-14 10:01 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 ramp: short-term flexibility request for dedicated capacity

Sam — thanks for the note and the timeline. Looping in Capacity and Sales Ops to surface options. High-level reaction: we can consider a time-boxed porting/rotation approach but need to balance other commitments (existing reserved pools) and the automation overhead.

Proposed next steps (can you confirm dates for the eight windows?):
- We (Ops) evaluate whether we can carve a transient burst pool via porting 20% of a customer tranche for the requested windows.
- If carving isn't safe for stability, Ops proposes either temporary credits or a one-off SLA escalation to allow higher tail latency on those windows.
- We run a test canary for a single 6-hour window to validate orchestration and KV-cache behavior across model variants.

Marcus/Ben/Tessa — can you sketch feasibility and a rough impact matrix (cost, risk, and automation effort)? I attached a draft rotation plan for discussion.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rotation_plan_draft.pdf

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-09-14 14:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 ramp: short-term flexibility request for dedicated capacity

Evelyn — quick feasibility notes after an ops review:
- Technical constraints: porting a fraction of a dedicated tranche mid-run has two impacts: (1) KV cache miss amplification for the model family if we move VMs/GPU instances between pools, and (2) scheduling churn which increases latency tail for both the donor and recipient pools during the transition window.
- Mitigations: we can limit transitions to non-overlapping windows and prefer instance-level handoffs that preserve local SSD and cache pinning (minimizes KV cold starts). That reduces the effective burst capacity we can present (realistic number is closer to 12–15% for safe ops vs 20%).
- Ops effort: we need ~3 engineering person-days to automate porting for repeatable windows and one pre-production rehearsal run. Manual orchestration is possible but risky and requires on-call coverage during each window.
- Risk matrix: if we proceed with automated porting, risk score is medium; manual porting is high.

Suggested language for the customer: we offer a time-boxed "rotation window" plan: 12–15% ephemeral capacity available for up to 8 windows, with a single canary run before calendar-wide activation. If BrightEdge needs full 20% guaranteed, we recommend an overprovisioned short-term commit (reserved) or credit-based compensation.

Marcus Lin
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example>, Sam Liao <sam@brightedge.com>
Date: 2027-09-15 08:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 ramp: short-term flexibility request for dedicated capacity

Sam — thanks for laying this out. Two commercial levers that will make this cleaner:
1) Rotation credit: provide BrightEdge a one-time pool of credits that can be used to subsidize the extra system cost when we spin up burst capacity for their windows. Credits are simpler contractually than a short-term reserved addendum.
2) Priority rotation schedule: we publish a set of 8 agreed windows; during those windows BrightEdge is placed in a soft-priority rotation for burst slots (not a hard preemption of other paid commitments). If we hit simultaneous conflicts, we apply the rotation fairness algorithm (round-robin across customers who opt-in).

Attachment: BrightEdge_throughput_profile.csv

Action items: Evelyn to confirm dates, Marcus to confirm automation estimate, Ops to do a canary run on the first requested window, Sales to publish credits proposal.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Sam Liao <sam@brightedge.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-09-15 12:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 ramp: short-term flexibility request for dedicated capacity

Appreciate the clarity. Confirming the windows below (all 6-hour windows, PST):
- 2027-10-05 00:00–06:00
- 2027-10-12 18:00–00:00
- 2027-10-20 02:00–08:00
- 2027-11-03 16:00–22:00
- 2027-11-09 00:00–06:00
- 2027-11-14 20:00–02:00
- 2027-11-21 04:00–10:00
- 2027-11-28 18:00–00:00

We prefer the 20% number but okay to accept 12–15% for the canary and trial phase. If we need credits, we'll take the credits option. Can we get a written note that the rotation schedule won't be used to preempt our baseline reserved slots outside the agreed windows? That's a non-starter for us.

Sam

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
To: Sam Liao <sam@brightedge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-09-16 17:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Q4 ramp: short-term flexibility request for dedicated capacity

Team — summary and decision:
- Offer: implement a "rotation window" program for BrightEdge for the eight dates Sam listed. For the canary (2027-10-05) we will provision up to 15% ephemeral capacity under automated porting. After canary validation, we will target a 15% rolling burst for the remaining windows.
- Commercials: Sales will provide BrightEdge with a credit pool to offset the incremental cost for burst runs. This avoids amending the reserved contract. Credits terms: one-time, non-refundable, applied to burst usage only. Ben will draft language.
- Non-preemption guarantee: BrightEdge baseline committed tranche will not be preempted outside of agreed rotation windows. During windows, we use soft-priority rotation (round-robin fairness) — documented and visible via Console logs.
- Risks & mitigations: Marcus will own the automation work (3 engineer-days) and run the canary with Ops on 2027-10-05 (engineer on-call assigned). Tessa will validate telemetry hooks so we can measure KV miss rates and tail latency during canary.
- Docs: I will publish the rotation plan and add the calendar entries to HubSpot. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8421

Please confirm acceptances and Ben, send the credits note by EOD Monday. Marcus/Tessa, confirm resource availability for the canary run. Sam, once you confirm acceptance of the canary terms we will mark the deal plan live.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rotation_plan_draft.pdf, BrightEdge_throughput_profile.csv
